summary.oneLiner: Infosys is a leading provider of AI-first business consulting and technology services, enabling organizations to unlock AI value at scale.
summary.business: Infosys provides AI-first business consulting and technology services to global enterprises, helping clients ideate, plan and scale their AI transformation by building strong data foundations with robust cloud capabilities. It serves clients across financial services, retail, manufacturing, communications, energy/utilities/resources, hi-tech, life sciences and public services, with delivery spanning North America, Europe, India and the rest of the world.

currentContext.strengths: More than four decades of experience managing the systems and workings of global enterprises|Early lead in AI, backed by an AI-first strategy and continued investment in AI capabilities|Proprietary intellectual property in software platforms and products (Infosys Cobalt for cloud, Infosys Topaz for agentic/generative AI, Infosys Aster for AI-amplified marketing)|Long-standing, trusted client relationships and a track record of execution, positioning Infosys as a navigator/orchestrator for clients' AI journeys
currentContext.strategies: Four-pronged strategy adopted since 2018 to strengthen client relevance and drive accelerated value creation: Scale Agile Digital, Energize the Core, Reskill our People, and Expand Localization.|AI-first value framework built on six interconnected value pools — AI Strategy & Engineering (Orchestrate), Data for AI (Insight), Process AI (Transform), Agentic Legacy Modernization (Modernize), Physical AI (Innovate) and AI Trust (Assure) — to help enterprises move from AI experimentation to enterprise-wide scale.|Two-pronged AI strategy: AI First Services to capture new demand and drive growth, and AI Augmented Services to reinvent existing offerings and win higher wallet share, underpinned by platforms/IP, ecosystem partnerships, talent and brand.|Positioning Infosys Topaz Fabric — a composable, interoperable AI agents/tools/services/models layer built on the AI-first value framework — as the core platform to operationalize AI at scale across data, applications, processes and systems.|ICETS (applied research) strategy focused on AI agent orchestration frameworks, automated model lifecycle transitions (LLM-to-SLM), and agent certification/governance to make AI execution enterprise-ready.|Brand strategy to position Infosys as the 'enterprise AI partner of choice', investing in global marketing partnerships (Australian Open, Roland-Garros, ATP, Madison Square Garden, ABB FIA Formula E, Dow Jones, Financial Times, etc.) and flagship client events (Confluence).|Leadership and talent strategy via the Infosys Leadership Institute (succession planning, leadership bench strength, title-holder development, inclusivity) and large-scale AI reskilling of the workforce.|Sustainability strategy centered on renewable energy expansion, green buildings, water stewardship (water-positive aspiration), zero-waste-to-landfill, and carbon-neutral events/offsets.
currentContext.expansion: As an asset-light IT services business, Infosys's capital expenditure during the year was directed mainly at computer equipment and infrastructure (additions to gross block of property, plant and equipment), and lease additions comprising computers and buildings taken on lease in certain locations outside India — there is no plant/manufacturing capacity expansion narrative. Growth capital was instead deployed toward acquisitions: the Company recognized ₹444 crore of consolidated goodwill during the year on the acquisition of MRE Consulting Ltd. and 'The Missing Link' group of entities (The Missing Link Security Pty. Ltd., The Missing Link Security Limited, and The Missing Link Automation Pty. Ltd.), funded via additional investment in subsidiaries for acquisition of entities, operations and expansions. On the sustainability infrastructure side, Infosys expanded on-site renewable generation to a total installed solar photovoltaic capacity of 62.42 MWp (a mix of rooftop- and ground-mounted systems) across its campuses, and extended its lake-rejuvenation program, raising cumulative water storage capacity from 6 billion litres to 10.3 billion litres (an addition of 4.3 billion litres of freshwater capacity).
currentContext.mdna: The traditional IT services market remains intensely competitive, driven by rapid technology change and the entry of new specialized players in technology niches.|AI is a transformational (not incremental) technology shift, compelling a foundational redesign of enterprise systems, architectures and operating models as organizations move from application-centric stacks to platforms with intelligent agents, orchestration layers and adaptive learning.|Businesses are increasingly using AI to deliver measurable outcomes — enhancing/personalizing customer interactions, improving marketing and sales efficiency, strengthening code quality, and boosting workforce/organizational productivity — expected to accelerate workforce transformation.|Management sizes an incremental AI-first services market opportunity of USD 300-400 billion by 2030 (per market estimates), which the company's AI-first value framework and Topaz platform are positioned to capture.|Client-centric growth: Infosys and its subsidiaries added 443 new clients during the year, growing the total client base to 1,965, with continued momentum in higher-value client bands (e.g., $100 million+ clients).|Company differentiators cited by management as driving competitive positioning: industry expertise, end-to-end service capabilities, scalable digital solutions, established platforms, quality/process excellence, distributed agile global delivery model, experienced leadership, skilled workforce and execution track record.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity threats in a hybrid-work operating model
risks.note: Employees operate in a hybrid model and the Information Security team must continuously monitor evolving global cybersecurity events; the Board constituted a dedicated Cybersecurity Risk Sub-Committee (under the Risk Management Committee, comprising only independent directors) to assess and enhance preparedness to mitigate cybersecurity risks, indicating this is treated as a top-tier structural risk.

Market capitalization-to-revenue and Price/Earnings ratios both moved adversely in fiscal 2026 because the share price fell by 20% even as revenue grew 9.6% and EPS grew 11.0%, indicating a widening gap between reported fundamental performance and market valuation.

risks.risk: Dependence on attracting and retaining skilled talent
risks.note: Management explicitly frames employees as the Company's 'most important assets' and its most important source of competitive advantage in AI-first consulting and technology services; as a labour-intensive services business, sustained ability to hire and retain best-in-class talent (and maintain a deep leadership pipeline) is structurally critical to delivery capability and growth.

one-line thesis: FY26 was a "resilience" year — US$20.2bn revenue (+3.1% CC), 21% adjusted margin, US$3.7bn FCF (112.6% of PAT), US$14.9bn large-deal TCV (55% net-new) — but the stock sits at a 52-week low (~₹1,030, down from ~₹2,000 last October) as the market prices an existential AI question ("if coding is automated, why are we needed?"). Management's whole answer is the AI-services pivot: an AI-first TAM of US$300–400bn by 2030, AI services already ~5.5% of revenue (~US$1bn annualized, growing faster than company average), Topaz Fabric + a partner ecosystem, and a FY27 guide of 1.5–3.5% CC growth at 20–22% margin. The near-term swing factors are soft discretionary demand + "AI inflation" (productivity deflation on legacy revenue); the long-term bet is that AI amplifies incumbents with deep enterprise context rather than replacing them.
financial scorecard (fy26, year ended ma: > One-offs: FCF optically down ₹1,400cr purely on FY25 tax-refund base effect, not operational. Reported margin cited is the adjusted 21%.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Revenue growth FY27: 1.5% to 3.5% constant currency — reaffirmed from the April 2026 results; excludes the Optimum acquisition completed this quarter.
Operating margin FY27: 20% to 22%. Medium-term "endeavour is to improve margins from current levels."
No guidance given for years beyond FY27 (CFO explicit).
AI-first services TAM: US$300–400bn addressable by 2030 across the six value pools (Nandan cited "close to $300bn IT spend by 2030"; CFO/Salil cited $300–400bn).
AI services run-rate: ~5.5% of revenue (~US$1bn annualized), growing faster than company average (metric last formally disclosed at Q3FY26; reconfirmed, not updated).
FY27 vertical outlook: acceleration expected in Financial Services, Energy/Utilities/Resources, and the Services grouping.
Hiring: plan to increase the number of college graduates brought in vs FY26's 20,000.
No new/changed capital-allocation or dividend policy — existing 85%-of-FCF policy runs through FY29.
order book & pipeline: FY26 large-deal TCV US$14.9bn, 55% net-new, deal wins +24% YoY. Beyond large deals, a broad book of medium/small deals.
Pipeline skewed to AI services + modernization; clients moving from AI pilots to enterprise-wide deployment. Rising AI-first GCC activity flagged as a conversion channel.
Demand environment described as soft / cautious on macro concerns; growth also dented by "AI inflation."
segment / vertical detail: FY26 above-company-average growth: Communications, Manufacturing, and Europe (all "significantly" above); Financial Services and the Services/Utilities/Energy/Resources grouping above average in CC.
FY27 acceleration expected: Financial Services; Energy/Utility/Resources; Services grouping.

M&A adds capability pockets: energy consulting (MRE), cybersecurity (Missing Link), Australia digital (Versent via Telstra JV), insurance/Guidewire (Stratus), US healthcare digital (Optimum Healthcare IT).
growth verticals / optionality: Six AI value pools ($300–400bn TAM to 2030): AI engineering & strategy; Data; Process/agents; Modernization (called out as the largest near-term area); Physical AI (manufacturing/medical/automotive); AI Trust.
Scale metrics: 90% of top-200 clients engaged on AI; 90% of employees "AI aware"; 4,800+ AI projects; 600+ agents built; forward-deployed-engineer team scaling; 16 analyst AI leadership rankings.
"Build vs buy" tailwind: AI has made legacy modernization urgent; clients retiring decades of technical debt and preferring to build — "creates even larger opportunities for us."

Innovation engine: Center for Emerging Technology & Solutions (incubating AI, ML, quantum), Infosys Living Labs (with universities in UK & US), Springboard digital skilling (15M reached in India; 10M+ worldwide free).
Optionality: quantum computing incubation; outcome-based / new pricing models being explored.
6a. moat & competitive position: Enterprise context / domain depth as the durable edge: "Enterprise context is paramount… tools are accelerators." Management's repeated thesis is that the value is combining agentic software with the traditional transaction systems clients already run — something AI platforms cannot do without an integrator. That "convergence is where the next wave of opportunities will emerge."

Owned IP + partner ecosystem: Topaz Fabric lets Infosys work with any foundation model; "all the big AI foundation-model companies and compute companies are working with Infosys" — foundation-model firms are "also approaching us."

Track record: organic growth fastest among peers for 7 consecutive years; FCF >100% of PAT two years running; world's most ethical company 6 years (Ethisphere); fastest-growing IT-services brand 6 years (Brand Finance).
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 margin held at 21% despite macro negatives, cross-currency drag, pyramid changes, and acquisition dilution — plus absorbed higher S&M/AI investment. (FY25 had expanded +50bps.)
Structural lever: revenue per employee rising; revenue growing faster than headcount via automation, pyramid and internal AI use (finance, marketing, coding).

"AI inflation" / productivity deflation is the acknowledged revenue headwind — client productivity savings are (partly) recycled into new IT spend, expanding the addressable market rather than pure leakage.
On AI margin question: management would not label AI margin-accretive/neutral/dilutive but pointed to the medium-term intent to lift margins.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Asset-light / no debt — no material capex program disclosed; balance sheet stays "very liquid."
Investment is in talent (20,000+ freshers, planning more in FY27), AI capability (Topaz Fabric), the partner ecosystem, and S&M expansion across geographies to widen TAM — not physical capex.
Location build-out: nearshore centers / digital studios / GCCs across Ahmedabad, Hubli, Visakhapatnam, Noida; Pocharam (Hyderabad) campus referenced by a shareholder (no capex detail given).
No capex earmarked for AI/quantum/data-centers — funded from existing cash, not leverage (directly answering a shareholder who feared debt-funded AI capex).
capital allocation: Policy: return ~85% of FCF cumulatively over the 5-year block FY25–FY29, via semi-annual dividends and/or buybacks/special dividends; progressively increasing DPS.
~₹55,000cr returned over the last two years; cumulative payout 82.1% of FCF over two years; FY25-26 payout incl. buyback = 113.9% of FCF.
₹18,000cr tender-offer buyback completed — management defends it as EPS-accretive and ROE-enhancing (against heavy shareholder criticism that it destroyed value / was tax-unfavourable).
M&A = disciplined tuck-ins to fill capability/segment white-spaces; strong cash gives speed on deals. Remaining ~15% of FCF funds these.
Bonus: last bonus was 2019; multiple bonuses historically; no bonus announced now (repeatedly requested by shareholders).
risks & watch-items: Existential AI narrative / "AI inflation": productivity deflation on legacy revenue; soft, cautious discretionary demand — the near-term growth swing.
CEO succession overhang: shareholder flagged Salil Parekh's term up for renewal next year as "an overhang that needs to be cleared" — notably NOT addressed in management's answers. Watch-item.
Stock at 52-week low (~₹1,029–1,030) vs ~₹2,000 last October; management "will not comment on share price."
Guidance itself is a low bar (1.5–3.5% CC) — a shareholder even asked for guidance to be scrapped (peer TCS gives none); CFO defended it as reducing information asymmetry.
Macro/geopolitics (Middle East, rates, FX) cited by shareholders; management leaned on 7-yr organic outperformance.
FCF base-effect (tax refunds) makes YoY cash-flow optics look worse than reality.
management quality / tone: Confident, measured, "resilience" framing; heavy emphasis that AI amplifies, not replaces incumbents with enterprise context. Nandan: "skate to where the puck is going… the puck is coming to where we have already positioned ourselves."
Transparent on the demand softness and "AI inflation"; candid that execution risk (reorienting services, sales, talent, pricing to AI-first) is the real risk, not opportunity availability.
Deflected two hot investor topics — CEO succession and share-price weakness — without direct answers. Strong governance signalling (unqualified audit, ethics awards, ESG detail).
non-obvious takeaways: AI revenue disclosure frozen: the 5.5%/~$1bn AI-services figure is a Q3FY26 number merely "reconfirmed" — no refreshed AI revenue metric a full year on, despite explicit shareholder demand to report AI revenue separately. Suggests either lumpiness or reluctance to reset the anchor.
Guidance excludes Optimum acquisition — so reported FY27 revenue will carry inorganic upside not in the 1.5–3.5% number.

Peer signalling on inorganic AI: a shareholder cited HCL investing in Sarvam AI and asked if Infosys would buy a major AI company; CFO stuck to tuck-in-only discipline — a deliberate strategic divergence from a peer.
"Build vs buy" flips the software-vendor threat into a services tailwind — enterprises retiring technical debt prefer to build, expanding the integrator's pie.
FCF "decline" is entirely a FY25 tax-refund base effect — not deterioration.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

hero.oneLiner: Infosys is a leading provider of AI-first business consulting and technology services, enabling organizations to unlock AI value at scale.
